claims.statement: For every finite passive observation design with q trajectories of duration T started at n0 below an unknown order m, the immigration-death network and its augmentation by mX -> (m+1)X can have total variation at most q Pr(Pois(T) >= m-n0), while the baseline is globally stable and positive recurrent and the augmented model is locally stable but deterministic finite-time explosive and CTMC explosive with positive probability.
assumptions: One species, unit-volume stochastic mass action, reactions ∅ -> X at rate 1 and X -> ∅ at rate 4
Augmented candidate adds mX -> (m+1)X at rate 1 with m >= 3
Observation starts at n0 < m, has finite duration T, and is passive until threshold m is reached
Candidate reaction order is not bounded in advance
claims.status: internally reconstructed theorem/counterexample; proof supplied in this report; not externally reviewed
claims.novelty_boundary: The hidden-tail construction is an explicit inference lower bound. It is non-endotactic and does not contradict the Astra N33 deterministic theorem. Standard coupling, Poisson tails, and birth-death explosion arguments are used; no historical priority claim is made.

costs.passive_data: q complete paths of duration T; divergence is possible only after first hitting m
costs.necessary_test_condition: For equal-prior average error <= epsilon, q >= (1-2epsilon)/Pr(Pois(T) >= m-n0)
costs.high_state_test: With ideal fixed at-risk exposure tau at n=m, threshold test error <= epsilon when tau >= 2 log(1/(2epsilon))/(sqrt(1+m!)-1)^2; preparation/reset costs are additional

claims.falsifier: Prepare/reset at n=m and measure the +1 event hazard. Baseline predicts 1; the augmented candidate predicts 1+m!. A resolved excess rejects the baseline; lack of excess only rejects the tested order/parameter candidate.
claims.next_gate: Audit the CTMC explosion proof and assess whether a realistic biological system permits controlled count-level excitation, direct event-channel resolution, and an independently justified maximum reaction order.

claims.statement: With known maximum source order N and complete exact transition-rate values for every transition vector on S_N={x in N_0^d: ||x||_1 <= N}, mass-action reaction-system structure and parameters are uniquely reconstructible by a triangular Newton/falling-factorial algorithm under its coefficient nonnegativity conditions; |S_N|=binom(N+d,d).
assumptions: Exact transition-rate map supplied on all states of S_N
Nonnegative Newton coefficients for each transition vector
claims.status: established primary-source theorem (Enciso–Erban–Kim 2021 paper, Theorem 3.1); finite-sample realization not included
claims.novelty_boundary: Exact finite rate-map identifiability is established prior work. This does not imply identifiability from an unbounded-order finite passive trajectory, nor does it decide global permanence or stochastic recurrence.

costs.data: Exact rates for all transition vectors at every state in S_N
costs.unaccounted_experimental_cost: State preparation/visits, event counts, rate-estimation precision and conditioning; no universal trajectory sample bound is claimed by Theorem 3.1

claims.falsifier: Under the stated exact data and order promise, a second distinct order-<=N mass-action system with the same complete rates on S_N would falsify uniqueness.
claims.next_gate: Specify an experimental state-acquisition protocol and derive a finite-sample confidence bound with explicit minimum rate separation and conditioning assumptions.

claims.statement: Astra N33's internally reconstructed all-endotactic measurable-rate permanence theorem applies only after the actual finite exponent-arrow diagram and positive rate box are supplied; Astra N35 gives finite-horizon stochastic exit control from a supplied strict inward polytope, not infinite-time stochastic permanence; Astra N50 is conditional and has no implemented general QE compiler.
assumptions: Claims are interpreted at their source-recorded status and exact interfaces
The current P/R package is treated as internal/source-reported evidence, not external proof certification
N76 and N77 are source-reported from a summary because their full original proof/code packet was unavailable
claims.status: source-status audit from pinned Astra commit; exact supplied originals selectively reconstructed
claims.novelty_boundary: The cited Astra research status is not external correctness or novelty validation. N33 is deterministic; N35's exact output is a finite horizon; N50 lacks a general implementation; N76/N77 original proof packets remain unavailable.

costs.N33_inputs: Finite actual diagram, class representative, and global positive rate interval; no observations acquired; no useful general bounds on family size, precision, cutoff, or waiting time
costs.N34_inputs: Supplied rational candidate and witnesses; budget exhaustion returns UNKNOWN; no arbitrary-unbounded-class global absorption synthesis established
costs.N35_inputs: Integer stoichiometry, certified inward collars/rate cap, volume V and buffered feasible lattice initial count; bound includes O(m V Lambda T exp(-c*V))
costs.N50_inputs: Rational actual endotactic network and rate box; QE/search costs unbounded and general compiler unimplemented
costs.N76_N77: Summary-only source reports; original proof/code unavailable

claims.falsifier: A verified counterexample to the N33 supplied deterministic interface or an all-time stochastic recurrence/nonexplosion theorem incorrectly claimed by the N35/N76/N77 statuses would change this scope assessment.
claims.next_gate: Obtain independent formal/external review of N33/R05; for stochastic claims prove physical-time nonexplosion and recurrence/tightness under the actual network, or retain UNKNOWN.
